source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed the primary System R access-path paper; PostgreSQL 18 EXPLAIN, index costing, multicolumn/skip-scan, bitmap combination, index-only, partition-pruning, and BRIN documentation; MySQL 8.4 range and index-merge documentation; current SQLite planner documentation; and current BigQuery clustered-table/block-pruning documentation. Checked predicate/bound/residual separation, access capabilities, order loss, visibility, pruning soundness, lossiness, current product scope, and cost inputs.

evidence: Checked R, q, c, p, feasible path set A, navigation bound, equality prefix, covering, correlation, parameterization, crossover, and regret definitions.
Checked access/index/residual/pruning predicates and identifier/page/row sets remain distinct.
Checked units for pages, rows, entries, bytes, startup/total, memory, and ordering properties.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Product-specific capabilities are not generalized to all index or storage methods.

evidence: Independently recomputed sequential 2250.00, point B-tree 37.14, medium plain 3339.50, bitmap 422.50, and broad index 5352.00.
Recomputed covering LIMIT 4.15, bitmap OR 270.00, pruned partition scan 225.00, and BRIN-like range 52.00.
Verified OR identifier union cardinality four and all intended path orderings with Decimal arithmetic.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Independent arithmetic is retained in artifacts/reviews/DBE-067/independent-recomputation.txt and does not import the chapter executable.

evidence: Reviewed Q subseteq B plus exact residual evaluation as the access-path correctness rule.
Reviewed composite equality-prefix/first-range structure and skip-scan union coverage.
Reviewed bitmap AND/OR set algebra, pruning emptiness proof, and multi-property dominance condition.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Lossy access is proven safe only as a superset followed by exact recheck; probability alone cannot justify exclusion.

evidence: Reviewed empty/all-row ranges, nulls/NaNs, open/closed boundaries, casts, expressions, collations, prefix/suffix gaps, duplicate OR IDs, and partial-index implication.
Reviewed MVCC visibility, stale/unknown/unsummarized/lossy metadata, disorder, partition defaults, schema evolution, encrypted/remote semantics, and row-level policies.

Reviewed LIMIT residual misses/ties, parameter repetition/skew, cache/correlation extremes, bitmap memory lossiness, remote failure/quota, OOD inputs, privacy, poisoned feedback, canaries, and rollback.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unknown metadata keeps candidate regions and mandatory visibility/security checks remain at the authorized layer.

evidence: Checked every path binds relation occurrence, snapshot/policy, predicates, columns, properties, parameter producers, capabilities, schema/index/statistics/model generations, and resource context.
Checked bounds never omit qualifying rows and every conservative/lossy candidate retains the exact residual/recheck.
Checked dominance preserves ordering, covering, startup, locality, parameterization, memory, uncertainty, and fallback distinctions.
invariant_checking.notes: Semantic feasibility precedes costing and local path cost cannot stand in for whole-plan value.

evidence: Reviewed the superset-and-recheck equality proof.
Reviewed composite interval and skip-scan correctness arguments.
Reviewed bitmap union deduplication, pruning impossibility, and property-aware dominance reasoning.
proof_review.notes: No universal sargability, exact synopsis, heap-free covering, stable crossover, or globally optimal path is claimed.

evidence: The executable is labeled normalized finite equations rather than a named-engine benchmark.
Pruning and residual claims distinguish exact proof, conservative bound, lossy summary, implementation mechanism, and policy.
PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, BigQuery, and System R statements are scoped to their cited versions/interfaces.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current practice, formal invariants, cost models, empirical evidence, and rollout policy remain separate.

evidence: Repository verification passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact nineteen-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and Python 3.14.4 toolchain.
Independent Decimal recomputation reproduced nine costs, path comparisons, OR-set cardinality, and superset-recheck identity.
All twelve source artifacts were retained under artifacts/references/DBE-067 and local Markdown links were checked.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live DBMS access-path execution, MVCC/visibility test, lossy index, remote/columnar source, workload replay, security test, canary, or external review was run.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed capability discovery, predicate classification, composite/skip/partial/expression matching, sequential/index/covering/bitmap/pruning/remote paths, ordering, parameterization, dominance, uncertainty, diagnosis, and evaluation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed snapshot/security binding, visibility and heap-fetch evidence, bitmap/pruning/resource behavior, parameter and remote contexts, first-divergence diagnosis, hints as temporary controls, shadowing, canaries, observability, privacy, kill switches, and rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter derives selection from sound bounds and properties, executes nine finite decisions, covers fourteen misconceptions and ten distinct examples, and advances five exercises to an elite validation/rollout design with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external database researcher, optimizer/index maintainer, MVCC reviewer, distributed-storage operator, security/privacy reviewer, platform owner, or educator review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither matching correctness for arbitrary SQL/access methods, pruning soundness of a live system, visibility correctness, accurate cost/cardinality estimates, global plan optimality, representative performance, privacy, fairness, certification, nor deployment fitness.
